analysis.title: "Buy The Rumor, Sell The News": Wilson Says The Correction Needs One Last Flush To 7,100 Before The Year-End Rally
key_insights: Morgan Stanley's Mike Wilson says the correction that began in June is entering its final phase as the S&P 500 catches down to breadth and approaches the firm's 7100-7300 downside range. A retest of last week's lows likely sets up a year-end rally.

Wilson recommends adding quality cyclicals with strong EPS revisions as the market carves out a low, and Industrials on an equal-weighted basis (relative revisions held up, ISM backlog broadening, Cass Freight shipping growth improving for the first time in nearly four years).

The SOX is down about 40% since June and is tracking Morgan Stanley's silver-stock analog (silver shifted forward four months). The analog implies chips are close to done falling but that the first bounce gets sold, with Monday's SOX gain of 6.85% cited as a caution.

Morgan Stanley expects a marginal new low below last week's lows on lower momentum, in the 7,100-7,300 range, as a classic re-test. ZeroHedge calculates this as a 3.3% to 6% drop from Monday's close of 7,550.

The spread between the S&P's distance from its 200-day average and the share of members above their 200-day average is down to 2%, after Thursday's 4.4% plunge (worst day since Liberation Day). The index has largely caught down to breadth.

Wilson's sentiment indicator fell last week but is still above the March lows and not at a washout. Equity vol spiked to where bond vol has been, and Morgan Stanley's Global Risk Demand Index is nearer to past-low extremes. Thursday was the biggest put day in Cboe history.

Goldman's prime book US long/short net leverage fell to 43.3%, the lowest in five years, after the biggest weekly gross cut since Covid. Goldman's futures strategists model CTAs as sellers of S&P futures this week in every scenario, about $31BN in a flat tape, with a long-term CTA pivot at 7,084.

On data center risk, Wilson says 2027 data center capex is 5% of consensus S&P 500 revenue and mid-single digits in 2028, so the index impact is limited and more than priced at 18x forward earnings (about Liberation Day valuation). Goldman sees state-level moratoria that could freeze about 45% of planned US capacity.

Wilson lists three potential positives after the midterms: lower oil on hopes of an Iran deal, a possible reversal of SNAP and Medicaid cuts, and a possible pull-forward of business activity and M&A before the 2028 election. Markets historically trade well in the 6-12 months after midterms.

Wilson's wildcard is a Fed that stays more hawkish than expected, which would drag the bottoming process into December. He compares the situation to late 2018, Powell's first year as chair, versus Warsh's first year now with a more hawkish FOMC.

Fed Governor Waller said Tuesday he leans toward a 25bp December hike and that 50bp should be on the table if core CPI came in around 0.3% or higher. Core CPI then printed around that level. A December hike is fully priced with 14% odds of 50bp.

Michelle Weaver's LLM screen of about 18,000 transcripts finds 44% of S&P 500 companies cited a quantifiable AI benefit over the trailing 12 months, up from 32%. Financials lead at 67% (from 42%), Communication Services 61%, Tech 51%.
AI-related costs are now cited by 22% of S&P companies, up from 8%. Token, inference and API charges are the biggest category at 51% (from 15%), overtaking compute and infrastructure at 26%.
Morgan Stanley's AI Adoption Leaders list: BAC, JPM, V, EBAY, UNH, PG, LOW, RTX. Wilson's highest-conviction theme into 2027 is AI adoption rather than AI infrastructure.

With roughly 90% of the index reported, Q3 EPS is tracking +30% y/y on 13% sales growth. Consensus has 2026 and 2027 earnings growth at 33% and 16%. EPS surprise is 3.9% vs a 4.4% historical average and Q2's 26%.
Earnings revisions breadth is +10%, well off summer highs. Net EPS revisions for covered stocks were +15%, half of Q2's +30%. The median stock moved 0.0% the day after results.

Of Q2's 53% S&P net income growth, about 27 points was non-operating profit, largely unrealized gains on private AI investments. Consensus has S&P net income growth at 1% in Q2 2027 versus 22% excluding non-operating income.
S&P 493 is expected to outgrow the Mag 7 in 2027 (16% vs 12%), and the Mag 7 share of index earnings growth is set to fall from 49% this year to 24%.

Free cash flow surprises moved stocks more than EPS surprises this quarter: a second-best-quintile FCF beat was worth 3.3% relative performance the next day vs 1.7% for the equivalent EPS beat. In the top bucket it was 1.4% vs 0.5%.

ZeroHedge's own view is that Wilson's risk case is the one to bet on. A retest on lower momentum needs tired sellers, but core CPI at 0.3%, a Fed governor discussing 50bp, a locked-in December hike and CTAs selling into strength supply new sellers. Morgan Stanley's buy level and Goldman's CTA flip level (7,084) are about the same number.

tension_points.bull_case: Morgan Stanley sees a re-test of 7100-7300 on lower momentum marking the end of the correction, followed by a rally into year-end and 2027. Positioning is clean (Goldman net leverage at a five-year low) and the equity-bond vol gap has closed.
tension_points.bear_case: ZeroHedge argues a re-test on lower momentum needs tired sellers, but a hawkish Fed (Waller on 50bp, December hike priced) and CTAs selling into strength supply fresh sellers. The last first-year Fed chair to ignore the market into year-end saw the low on Christmas Eve.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Fed that stays more hawkish than expected would drag the bottoming process into December. Goldman's CTA pivot at 7,084 sits at the bottom of Morgan Stanley's buy zone.

tension_points.bull_case: Wilson says data center capex is 5% of consensus S&P 500 revenue in 2027 and mid-single digits in 2028, so the index hit is limited and priced at 18x forward earnings.
tension_points.bear_case: Goldman sees state-level moratoria that could freeze about 45% of planned US capacity. The 5% share is less comforting for companies for which it is the whole order book, or for the bonds that financed them.

tension_points.bull_case: 44% of S&P 500 companies cite a quantifiable AI benefit, up from 32%, and the top decile of companies that quantify benefits see forward earnings rise well ahead of the S&P.
tension_points.bear_case: 22% of S&P companies cite AI-related costs, up from 8%, with token, inference and API charges the biggest category at 51%.
